status.en: 7 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 30% fewer than the week before, most of them in Mogadishu, Puntland and Isaaq.
status.nb: 7 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 30 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Mogadishu, Puntland og Isaaq.

summary.en: Somali federal forces and U.S. airstrikes have recently killed dozens of al-Shabaab militants in Lower Shabelle, while a Turkish-made missile strike killed a Somali family in Puntland, linking the conflict to external weapon supplies. The Somali government warned that Houthi support could boost al-Shabaab attack capabilities, and the parliament speaker accused Kenya, Ethiopia and Uganda of colluding with the group, while the president blamed the UAE for financing armed groups. Foreign troops are beginning to withdraw, raising concerns that al-Shabaab could expand its influence. The conflict caused 2,284 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Somaliske føderale styrker og amerikanske luftangrep har nylig drept dusinvis av al-Shabaab-militante i Lower Shabelle, mens et tyrkiskprodusert missilangrep drepte en somalisk familie i Puntland, og knytter konflikten til eksterne våpenforsyninger. Den somaliske regjeringen advarte om at houthiene kan øke al-Shabaabs angrepskapasitet, og parlamentets talsperson anklaget Kenya, Etiopia og Uganda for å samarbeide med gruppen, mens presidenten la skylden på De forente arabiske emirater for å finansiere væpnede grupper. Utenlandske tropper begynner å trekke seg tilbake, noe som gir bekymring for at al-Shabaab kan utvide sin innflytelse. Konflikten forårsaket 2 284 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.extract: The ongoing phase of the Somali Civil War began in 2009 and is concentrated in southern and central Somalia, primarily between the forces of the Federal Government of Somalia (FGS), assisted by African Union peacekeeping forces, and the Islamist militant group al-Shabaab, which pledged allegiance to al-Qaeda in 2012.
